questions.prompt: What should guide the choice of a PostgreSQL data type?
options: Whether the type removes the need for validation.
The value semantics, supported operations, precision and constraints required by the application.
The shortest type name regardless of the data.
The assumption that all values should be text.
questions.answer_key: The value semantics, supported operations, precision and constraints required by the application.
questions.explanation: Correct data types improve semantic clarity and allow PostgreSQL to enforce and operate on values appropriately.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports a correct implementation of practical query patterns?
options: Define the expected behavior and prerequisites, make the smallest change in an isolated environment, then verify both success and an important edge case.
Concatenate user input into SQL and remove permission checks
Assume one successful example proves security and recovery
Apply the largest possible change before collecting a baseline
questions.answer_key: Define the expected behavior and prerequisites, make the smallest change in an isolated environment, then verify both success and an important edge case.
questions.explanation: A controlled example makes the prerequisites and expected behavior explicit. Verification of an edge case helps show whether the idea behind practical query patterns is understood.

questions.prompt: When an example related to practical query patterns produces an unexpected result, what is the strongest next step?
options: Disable constraints and retry until the command succeeds
Grant administrator privileges to every application role
Ignore the returned result and assume the write succeeded
Capture the exact error and context, inspect relevant state or logs, test one hypothesis at a time, and document the verified result.
questions.answer_key: Capture the exact error and context, inspect relevant state or logs, test one hypothesis at a time, and document the verified result.
questions.explanation: Database troubleshooting should be evidence-led and performed with suitable permissions. Broad privileges or disabling integrity checks may hide the cause and create new failures.
